editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Sustain = sustain pedal on a piano, keeping the sound continuous over time.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Continued or kept in existence without interruption over an extended period.

editorials.title: AI can kill humanity in a decade? Get in line

editorial_metadata.title: AI can kill humanity in a decade? Get in line
editorial_metadata.subtitle: Growing apocalyptic threats have normalised catastrophic risks, leaving humanity indifferent to emerging dangers.
editorial_metadata.author: Editorial Board

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Think of 'all is done, but a tiny bit remains'—meaning very nearly or almost completely.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Very nearly or to such an extent that any difference is negligible.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: When you run fast and catch up to someone ahead, you reach their level.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Reached the same standard, pace, or condition as something that was ahead.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Opposite of 'utopia' (ideal place); 'dys-' signifies bad or diseased society.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Imagined states or societies characterised by great suffering, oppression, or terror.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Relate to 'reveal'—a dramatic uncovering or making known of a secret.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: A surprising and previously unknown or secret fact that has been disclosed.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Gambling in a casino means betting and risking valuable money on uncertainty.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: To take reckless risks with something precious, relying on chance.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: If everyone moves forward and you stay behind, you are left trailing.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Failing to maintain the same rate of progress or success as competitors.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Existential relates to 'existence'—a danger so severe that existence itself could end.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: A peril that jeopardises the continued very existence or survival of an entity.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Rhymes with 'cuss about'—making noise and getting agitated over trivial matters.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Excessive, unnecessary excitement, worry, or protest over something.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Doom + Day = the ultimate final day when utter ruin or destruction arrives.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: The time of the total destruction of the world, or final judgment.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Think of 'past'—something that belongs to the past and is no longer fashionable.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: No longer fashionable, interesting, or relevant; hopelessly out of date.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Think of the enormous ship 'Titanic' or the powerful Greek Titans of immense strength.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Persons or organisations of exceptionally enormous power, influence, or ability.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Brink sounds like 'blink'—stand on the edge of a cliff and one blink could drop you.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: The critical point at which a new, often hazardous or disastrous situation is imminent.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Apocalypse contains 'collapse'—a giant cosmic collapse ending humanity.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: An event involving widespread and devastating destruction, heralding the end of the world.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Not 'famous' in a good sense, but famous for 'in-' (negative/evil) deeds.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Well known for some exceptionally bad deed, quality, or sinister association.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Moving forward by single inches at a time—advancing very slowly and steadily.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Moving or progressing by very small, slow, and gradual stages towards a point.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Literally joining a queue behind many others who are already waiting ahead of you.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: To wait one's turn among many competing claims or issues; to not be uniquely special.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Mass (collective people) + psychosis (mental disorder) = collective madness.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: A condition where a large segment of society simultaneously exhibits irrational or delusional behaviour.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Sounds like 'imperil' or 'perish'—if you fall into peril, you may perish.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: Serious and immediate danger of injury, ruin, or catastrophe.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: Banality comes from 'banal' (boring, ordinary)—thinking a grave danger is just plain and boring.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: The state of being so common, unoriginal, and ubiquitous as to be unremarkable.

editorial_vocabulary.mnemonic_trick: From Latin 'mors' meaning death; 'mortal' beings are destined to die.
editorial_vocabulary.concise_meaning: The condition of being susceptible to death; the inevitable end of living existence.
